info.longBusinessSummary: Elixirr International plc, through its subsidiaries, provides management consultancy services in the United Kingdom, the United States, and internationally. It provides services in the areas of AI and machine learning, app design and development, brand identity implementation, brand strategy and positioning, breakthrough imperatives, business and operating modes, business strategy, change management, corporate culture, corporate venture and innovation, customer experience, data and analytics, data strategy, define the C-suite agenda, digital design and build, digital marketing, digital optimization and strategy, enterprise-wide transformation, executive immersions, generative AI, IT strategy, mergers and acquisitions, managed services, onboarding solutions, procurement, product and portfolio management, risk and compliance, sourcing and commercial office, sustainability, target operating model, and transformation management, and transformational leadership. The company serves automotive and transportation, manufacturing, business and financial services, charities, energy, oil and gas, utilities and power, private equity, retail and corporate banking, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, insurance, luxury and fashion, wealth and asset management, wholesale banking, travel and leisure, telecommunications, technology, retail and consumer goods, media, and entertainment and sports industries. Elixirr International plc was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in London, the United Kingdom.

rationale.growth: Years 1–2 from analyst consensus (5 analysts: 20.7%, 7.2%); then a straight-line fade to 2.5% terminal growth by year 7.
rationale.ebit_margin: Starts at last year's EBIT margin (19.1%) and moves to the 4-year median (22.5%) over 5 years.
rationale.tax: Median effective tax rate (25.2%), kept within 15–30%.
rationale.reinvestment: Historical medians: D&A 3.9%, capex 0.2% of revenue; working capital -12.0% of revenue, so each extra $1 of sales ties up $-0.12. Stock-based compensation (2.3% of revenue) stays inside GAAP EBIT and is not added back, so it is treated as a real cost. IFRS reporters: lease payments sit in financing cash flow, so check capex covers them.
rationale.wacc: CAPM: risk-free 4.50% (Fallback assumption (FRED IRLTLT01GBM156N unavailable)) + adjusted beta 0.83 × ERP 5.0% + small-cap premium 1.0% = cost of equity 9.67%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.50% (interest ÷ debt). Market-value weights: debt 12.7%.
rationale.exit_multiple: Median peer EV/EBITDA (9.5x) as a cross-check terminal value.
